newsitem.title: UK: London spot platinum indicated at high since 1990.
newsitem.headline: London spot platinum indicated at high since 1990.

text.p: Spot platinum was quoted at $480.00/$510.00 in early European trading on Friday, the highest level since 1990, dealers said.
It had closed at $430.00/$440.00 in London on Thursday.

Prices for platinum and its sister metal palladium have been soaring since the start of the year because of protracted delays in exports from major producer Russia and a build-up of speculative fund holdings of the metal.
Supply tightness and price volatility have become increasingly severe in recent days and market makers on Thursday held an emergency meeting to promote order in the market.

"The market is in a bit of a panic. Nobody is buying at this level if they can help it. But there are people who have positions due this week and next who are forced to buy it here," a European based bullion dealer said.
Palladium, which has been trading at the highest levels since 1980 this week, was bid at $235.00/$245.00 an ounce, after closing at $205.005/$215.00 on Thursday.
